everyone.title: Everyday use
everyone.desc: Set up, find and copy passwords, organize, and keep everything safe.

slides.title: Your passwords, on locked pages
slides.text: Vaultleaf keeps every account on its own page, encrypted on your device before anything is saved. This tour takes about three minutes. Use the arrows, swipe, or press the arrow keys.

slides.title: Set up: a password, then a passcode
slides.text: Choose a master password of at least 10 characters, then a 4, 6 or 8 digit passcode. Together they unlock your vault.
points: A few random words make a strong password. Tap Suggest a passphrase if you like.
Use a passcode that isn't your phone's code.

slides.title: Save your recovery key
slides.text: If you ever forget your password or passcode, this key is the only way back in. Nobody can reset your vault for you, not even an admin.
points: Copy or download it, then keep it away from this device.
You can make a new one later in Settings.

slides.title: Unlock, and it locks itself
slides.text: Each time, type your password, then your passcode on the keypad. Vaultleaf locks after 5 minutes without activity, or when it's in the background for a minute.
points: After 5 wrong tries you wait 30 seconds, then longer.
Lock any time with the lock button.

slides.title: Face ID or fingerprint
slides.text: Turn it on in Settings, under Security, to unlock without typing on this device. Your password and passcode are still asked for every 14 days.

slides.title: Find your way around
slides.text: Sections are on the left on a computer and at the bottom on a phone. Search finds names, usernames, emails, websites, labels and notes. Type #work to filter by a label.

slides.title: Copy, show and open
slides.text: Tap any line to copy it. The eye shows a hidden value and hides it again after 30 seconds. 2FA codes update every 30 seconds, ready to copy.

slides.title: Every change and copy is recorded
slides.text: Each account keeps its date stored, last edit, when the password was set, every copy with its time, and the old passwords and keys you replaced.

slides.title: Classic notes, or Modern cards
slides.text: Classic looks like the notes app you keep passwords in now: folders, notes by date, one detail per line. Modern shows cards with copy buttons. Switch with the two icons above the list.

slides.title: Write an account like a note
slides.text: In Classic view, Add and Edit open a plain text page. The first line is the name, then one Label: value per line. Vaultleaf turns the lines into fields and hides passwords, PINs and keys.

slides.title: Add an account
slides.text: Pick what it is, like a website login, crypto wallet or bank card, and the right fields are ready. Generate fills in a strong password.

slides.title: Keys, phrases, questions and admins
slides.text: Add PINs, API keys, secret phrases and 2FA setup keys, security questions with hidden answers, and the people who manage the account with their emails and roles.

slides.title: Labels and sub-labels
slides.text: Labels work like folders, but an account can have several. Type Work/Cloud to make a sub-label. Picking a parent shows everything inside it.

slides.title: Bring over your notes
slides.text: Paste your notes into Settings, Import from Notes. Put a line with --- between notes to bring many at once. CSV files from browsers and other managers work too.

slides.title: Attach files
slides.text: Keep ID scans, recovery sheets or contracts on the account they belong to. Each file is encrypted, up to 5 MB, and syncs with the rest.

slides.title: Make strong passwords
slides.text: Random characters or real-word passphrases, with a strength rating. Use for an account puts the new password straight into an account.

slides.title: Password health
slides.text: Health points out weak, reused and overdue passwords. Tap one to open the account and change it.

slides.title: Check for leaked passwords
slides.text: On the Health page, Check my passwords looks for each one in public breach lists. Only 5 characters of a scrambled fingerprint are sent, never the password.

slides.title: Activity
slides.text: Every copy and change across all accounts, with the time. Tap an event to open its account.

slides.title: Settings
slides.text: Change your password, passcode or recovery key, choose when Vaultleaf locks, and pick the view and theme.

slides.title: Sync your phone and computer
slides.text: Turn on sync in Settings and copy your sync code. On the other device, choose Use my vault from another device, paste the code and unlock as usual.
points: Edits on two devices are combined.

slides.title: Back up
slides.text: Settings, Back up saves an encrypted file you can keep anywhere. Restore it on any device with the password and passcode you had, or your recovery key.

slides.title: Recently deleted
slides.text: Deleted accounts stay here for 30 days, so you can restore them.

slides.title: Emergency kit for someone you trust
slides.text: Make a file with everything, or only some labels, that opens with its own code. Give the file and the code to your trusted person separately.

slides.title: Put it on your home screen
slides.text: On iPhone, open Vaultleaf in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. On Android, use Chrome's menu, then Install app. It then opens full screen and works offline.

slides.title: Find this tour again
slides.text: Take the tour any time from Settings or the Guide. After each update, What's new shows only what changed. The full illustrated guide has every detail.

admin.title: For admins
admin.desc: Run the Vaultleaf website: access, updates, sync storage and helping people.

slides.title: You run the website, not the vaults
slides.text: Admins look after the Vaultleaf site on Vercel, its code on GitHub and its sync storage on Supabase. Every vault stays with its owner: nobody, including you, can see or reset one.

slides.title: Choose who can open the site
slides.text: In Vercel, open mco-vault-leaf, then Settings, then Deployment Protection. With Vercel Authentication on, only people in your Vercel team can open the site. Off, anyone with the link can, and each gets their own empty vault.

slides.title: Publish an update
slides.text: Change the source in vault-leaf/src of c3jumpw/mco and push to main. Vercel deploys it, and the docs workflow then retakes every screenshot and rebuilds this tour and the guide.

slides.title: Roll back if something breaks
slides.text: In Vercel, open the project's Deployments, pick the last good one and choose Instant Rollback. People's saved data is never touched by updates or rollbacks.

slides.title: Look after sync storage
slides.text: Synced vaults sit encrypted in the MKC-Admin Supabase project, tables vaultleaf_vaults and vaultleaf_blobs. You can see how many sync and their size, never their contents. Deleting a row stops that vault's sync.

slides.title: Someone forgot their password
slides.text: They choose Forgot your password or passcode on the unlock screen and enter their recovery key. Without it, a recent backup file is the only way back. You can't reset a vault.

slides.title: Someone has a new phone
slides.text: With sync on, they open Vaultleaf on the new phone, choose Use my vault from another device and enter the sync code from Settings on their old device. Without sync, they restore a backup file.

slides.title: This tour updates itself
slides.text: Each push that changes Vaultleaf runs a GitHub workflow that rebuilds the app, retakes every screenshot, rebuilds the tour and guide, and fails if a new feature has no slide or guide section.
